summary: Phra Sigambhirayan specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan works in Buddhist studies. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
Phramaha Somboon Watana works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Panjab University in 1999, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma.

Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) under supervisor Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle. He also studied under Jeff Wilson and traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.

Phuntshok Tashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (B.A) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (MA), and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Radcliffe and Harvard (PhD ~1973), she held professorships at McMaster (~1976-2004) and Yale (~2004-2021), with roles at Berkeley, Paris, and Toronto Mississauga.

Pierce Salguero is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (~2005-2010), later holding posts at Pennsylvania State University (2010) and the University of Pennsylvania (2011-2012).

Pierre Amédée Jaubert was a linguist who studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1795-1798). He later held posts there (~1838-1847), at the Collège de France (1838-1847), and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1834-1847).
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen specializes in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University by 1991, where he also held a post as a research fellow (attested 1996).

Pieter Hendrik Pott was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served as a curator at the Museum Volkenkunde (~1947-1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.
Pietro Merlo was a linguist who studied under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin (~1868-1872). He later held an academic post at the University of Pavia from ~1881 to 1888.

Piotr Balcerowicz is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. Educated at Warsaw, Banaras Hindu, and Hamburg universities, he earned his habilitation from the Polish Academy of Sciences in 2005 and served on the editorial board at the University of Warsaw (~2000-2005).

Piotr Klafkowski was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University under Jerzy Bańczerowski, and studied under teachers Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche, and Nyalo Trulku Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka was an Indonesian scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1921-1926) and later held a post at the University of Indonesia (~1950-1964).

Poh Beng Tan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College (attested 2015). The degree was supervised by Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, and Tan also studied under Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar in Buddhist studies and related fields. She completed her studies at Goddard College, Ohio University, and Washington University in St. Louis.
Pori Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held an appointment at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and served as a professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 2009).

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Krishnagar Government College and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, he held posts at the University of Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.

Prafulla Chandra Ray worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Vidyasagar College, Presidency University, and the University of Edinburgh (~1882-1888), he held posts at Presidency University (1911-1916) and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture (1916-1936).
